html:
Kanara is the coast of Karnataka along the Arabian Sea, from Karwar down to Mangalore. On the 1800 map it has just passed to the British.

Behind the coast, the Keladi Nayakas ruled from Ikkeri and Bednore after Vijayanagara fell, trading rice and pepper through its ports. In 1763 Hyder Ali of Mysore took Bednore and the coast. The Treaty of Mangalore in 1784 ended his son's second war with the British. Tipu Sultan then had tens of thousands of the region's Catholics marched inland as captives, and many died.

After Tipu's death in 1799 the British took Kanara. It was later split: North Kanara went to the Bombay Presidency and South Canara, around Mangalore, to the Madras Presidency. The town of Banavasi, inland, had been the capital of the Kadambas long before.
sum: Kanara is the coast of Karnataka along the Arabian Sea, from Karwar down to Mangalore. On the 1800 map it has just passed to the British.
